newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - UK's Hardy sees 1997 take-off.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - UK's Hardy sees 1997 take-off.

text.p: Britain's Hardy Oil and Gas Plc will launch itself firmly into a growth phase this year as it has a new management team in place after a two-year period of asset restucturing, the group's chief executive said on Monday.
"I think we will lift off this year," chief executive John Walmsley told Reuters.
Walmsley took over the helm at Hardy early in 1995 and has since then replaced nearly all senior management, while drastically pruning operations to boost the company's financial health.
"This industry is unforgiving for the financially unprepared," said Walmsley, who was one of the founding directors of Enterprise Oil Plc which he left in 1993.
Under Walmsley, Hardy sold off assets in Canada and the U.S., while it also withdrew from Algeria, Libya, Namibia and the Netherlands.
The junior exploration firm's main interests are now in the North Sea, the Timor Sea, West Australia, Pakistan and India.
In the past two years, Hardy has brought down its gearing to seven percent from 47 percent by end-1994 and is now ready to deliver growth.
"We will demonstrably add value," Walmsley said.

Three months ago, Hardy reported a net profit over the nine months to December, 1996 of 5.7 million stg, which compared with a 6.6 million loss in the year to March 1996. Previously, the company said it would change its year-emd from March 31 to December 31.
Walmsley declined to name specific medium-term targets Hardy has set itself, but said growth would come through a mix of exploration successes and acquisitions.
Earlier this year, the company cautiously moved onto the acquisition trail. In March, Hardy announced it had bought a 15.5 percent stake in Hindustan Oil Explorarion Company Ltd for 2.9 million stg.
Walmsley hopes to conclude bigger deals, but stresses Hardy won't buy at all costs, adding it is currently hard to find value for money in either the North Sea or Australia.
In the North Sea, Hardy has an eight percent interest in the large Elgin/Franklin gas field, which is under development. Gas sale negotiations were progressing "satisfactorily", Walmsley said.
The group's jewel in the crown, however, is the giant Bayu-Undan gas project in the Timor Sea.
Here, Hardy has a 15 percent interest in a venture led by Phillips Petroleum. Australia's BHP Petroleum leads the other venture developing the area.

The participants in Bayu-Undan, which is estimated to have proven and probable reserves of 3.1 trillion cubic feet, two months ago took a major step as they agreed BHP would be the project's sole operator.
Meanwhile, India is rapidly becoming another growth area for Hardy, which earlier this year reported drilling successes in the PY-3 oilfield off the Indian southeast coast.
Hardy is co-operating with HOEC in the field and recently bought interests in adjacent blocks as well. It aims to spend 25 million dollars this year on its Indian projects.
"This acreage has much more prospect than we thought," Walmsley said. "It is a classic potential core area," he added.
